A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoTHer research despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original VTHR recovery experiments, Llama 2 and Stable Diffusion case studies, and robustness analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 reports original recovery experiments and additional model-card, pruning, quantization, learning-rate, merged-parent and runtime analyses.

M1.justification: Equation 1 replaces the maximum weight-entry difference with an average of layerwise L2 distances, changing a central recovery component. Clustering changes from the stated L1 distance to L2 in the experimental setup. Appendix E adds preliminary two-parent detection using cosine similarity to cluster centers. The kurtosis-based direction score and directed spanning-tree framework remain.

E1.justification: V2 retains the VTAB-based training domains and Stable Diffusion case but removes Llama 2 lineage recovery. It adds recovery on mixed LoRA/full-fine-tuning populations, pruned and quantized models, merged-parent models, and a ResNet tree, plus large-scale model-card analysis. These extend the represented inputs and tasks beyond the VTHR-to-MoTHer renaming.

E2.justification: The mean-based directional-score comparator in v1 Figure 14 is removed from v2 Figure 8; variance, skewness and entropy remain alongside the proposed kurtosis score. The FT-distance alternative to the LoRA distance is retained. Neural Lineage is newly discussed as related work but is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Tables 2–3 replace fixed learning rates with four choices and change FT training from 5 epochs to 2–5 and LoRA training from 20 to 10–20 epochs. Recovery-layer selections also broaden. New protocols include a 121-model, five-level tree, pruning and quantization interventions, merged-parent detection and runtime scaling. The revised settings do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds deeper-tree scaling, pruning and quantization robustness, learning-rate/convergence sensitivity, merged-heritage exploration and runtime analysis. It removes v1's sampled smaller-tree recovery study and Table 4, while retaining the separate small-graph clustering analysis. The new studies substantially expand the questions tested about reliability and applicability.

E5.justification: V1's smaller-tree study reports ten random subtree samples per root and accompanying ± values; that study is removed. V2 instead reports ten randomized quantization repetitions with ± values in Table 5 and five distinct seeds per learning rate in Appendix D.3. These change statistical reporting for particular analyses, without establishing an increase in repetitions of retained experiments.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes FT graph accuracy from 0.89 to 0.94 under revised methods/settings, so this is not an established same-setting gain. New results include 0.79 recovery for the deeper tree, perfect ResNet recovery, and 0.68 accuracy at 99% pruning. Llama 2 and smaller-tree results disappear. V2's Mixed result is inconsistent: Table 1 reports graph accuracy 0.83, while the text reports 0.90 overall.

T1.justification: Equation 1 substantively changes the mathematical definition of the full-fine-tuning distance. Model Tree/Graph definitions, LoRA rank reasoning, kurtosis formulation and spanning-tree construction remain substantially unchanged. New Appendix G supplies conceptual motivation from cited mode-connectivity work, rather than a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claim that model weights enable heritage recovery remains. V2 adds the headline finding that roughly 60% of surveyed models lack informative heritage metadata, changes the claimed relationship from outlier distances to weight distances, and drops the explicit Llama 2 reconstruction claim. The 'unsupervised' renaming alone does not establish a new scientific claim.

C2.justification: V2 connects directional-score failures to non-convergent training and explains late-training noise through validation-loss plateaus. It explicitly discusses the single-parent limitation and preliminary merged-parent support, adds a mode-connectivity explanation for clustering, and revises the scalability discussion. These substantially expand the interpretation of mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies c = 0.3, pruning and quantization implementations, merged-model construction, cluster-center calculations and CPU/GPU timings, alongside revised hyperparameter tables. V1's min–max-normalization instructions disappear, without establishing that preprocessing actually stopped. A new reproducibility statement reports supplementary code and planned public code/data releases; actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 introduces Neural Lineage as the closest prior work and differentiates MoTHer through direction recovery, complex hierarchies and data-free computation. It adds weight-representation, model-merging and mode-connectivity literature, while removing earlier PCA, activation-interpretability and graph-metadata discussions. This substantively revises positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten around unsupervised model attribution. Experiments gain a dedicated setup subsection and reordered presentation; VTHR becomes MoTHer. Explanations and captions expand, and reproducibility and social-impact statements are added, producing substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 removes the Llama 2 diagram and smaller-tree table, moves and condenses directional-score plots into main-text Figure 8, and expands Table 1. It adds a model-card flowchart, pruning displays, a nine-panel learning-rate figure, and quantization, merged-parent and runtime tables. Core diagrams are retained within a substantially revised conference layout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence about practical reliability through mixed-training, deeper-tree, pruning and quantization tests, while the convergence analysis exposes failure conditions of the directional score. The metadata study and closer prior-work comparison also strengthen the motivation. These gains outweigh the loss of Llama 2 and smaller-tree evidence, although the conflicting Mixed accuracy in Table 1 and the text weakens that particular result.
